cities.name: Ghangaria

religious_cultural.name: Hemkund Sahib
religious_cultural.summary: Sacred high-altitude Sikh gurdwara situated at 14,107 ft beside a pristine glacial lake ringed by seven snow-clad peaks, revered as the meditation place of Guru Gobind Singh.

religious_cultural.opening_hours: 5:00 AM – 2:00 PM (all pilgrims must descend to Ghangaria by afternoon)
visitor_notes: Steep 6 km climb from Ghangaria; ponies and palanquins available
Brahma Kamal flowers can be seen along the trail

nature_parks_zoo.name: Valley of Flowers National Park
nature_parks_zoo.summary: UNESCO World Heritage alpine valley in the high Western Himalayas, blanketed in hundreds of rare wild alpine blooms, endemic medicinal flora, tumbling streams, and snowcapped cirques.
nature_parks_zoo.description: UNESCO World Heritage alpine valley in the high Western Himalayas, blanketed in hundreds of rare wild alpine blooms, endemic medicinal flora, tumbling streams, and snowcapped cirques.
nature_parks_zoo.best_time_to_visit: July to September (peak bloom in August)
nature_parks_zoo.entry_fee: ₹150 for Indians, ₹600 for foreigners (valid for 3 days)
nature_parks_zoo.opening_hours: 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM (entry closes by 2:00 PM; overnight stay prohibited)
visitor_notes: Requires a 14 km trek from Govindghat to Ghangaria, then 4 km to the valley
Carry rain gear, trekking poles, and pack out all trash

heritage.name: Srimanta Sankardev Kalakshetra
heritage.summary: Grand cultural institution showcasing the diverse indigenous arts and legacy of Saint Sankardev.

museums.name: Assam State Museum

museums.description: Established in 1940 by the Kamarupa Anusandhan Samiti, the Assam State Museum displays priceless collections of medieval stone sculptures, royal Ahom copper plate charters, medieval weapons, tribal textiles, and natural history specimens.

religious_cultural.name: Kamakhya Temple
religious_cultural.summary: One of the oldest and most revered Shakti Peethas in India, situated atop Nilachal Hill.
religious_cultural.description: Kamakhya Temple is the supreme centre of Tantric and Shakta worship in India. Dedicated to Mother Goddess Kamakhya, the shrine enshrines the sacred yoni rock sanctum through which a natural subterranean spring flows. Celebrated annually for the Ambubachi Mela.
religious_cultural.short_description: One of the oldest and most revered Shakti Peethas in India, situated atop Nilachal Hill.
religious_cultural.detailed_description: Kamakhya Temple is the supreme centre of Tantric and Shakta worship in India. Dedicated to Mother Goddess Kamakhya, the shrine enshrines the sacred yoni rock sanctum through which a natural subterranean spring flows. Celebrated annually for the Ambubachi Mela.
religious_cultural.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Ambubachi Mela in June)
religious_cultural.entry_fee: Free entry (VIP queue ₹501)
visitor_notes: Dress conservatively
Long queues on festival days

religious_cultural.name: Umananda Temple
religious_cultural.summary: Historic 17th-century Shiva temple situated on Peacock Island, the world’s smallest inhabited river island.
religious_cultural.description: Built in 1694 by Ahom King Gadadhar Singha, Umananda Temple sits on Peacock Island (Bhasmacala) in the middle of the Brahmaputra River. According to mythology, Lord Shiva burned Kamadeva to ashes here. Also home to endangered golden langurs.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Wildlife sanctuary holding the world’s highest ecological density of Greater One-Horned Rhinoceros.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Covering 38.8 square kilometers in the floodplains of the Brahmaputra, Pobitora is home to over 100 one-horned rhinos, wild boars, Asiatic buffaloes, and over 375 migratory and resident bird species in its vast wetlands.

nature_parks_zoo.description: Located along the Jia Bhoroli River in the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas, Nameri is a birder's paradise with over 300 bird species including four species of Hornbill and the critically endangered state bird of Assam, the White-Winged Wood Duck (Deo Hah).

cities.name: Majuli
cities.tagline: World’s Largest Inhabited River Island & Cradle of Neo-Vaishnavism
cities.description: Enchanting freshwater island in the mighty Brahmaputra River, cultural heart of Assam celebrated for 15th-century Vaishnavite Satras (monasteries), traditional mask making, and serene rural wetland landscapes.
cities.short_description: World’s largest river island, famous for 15th-century Vaishnavite Satras and mask making.

heritage.name: Majuli Island
heritage.summary: The world's largest inhabited river island, preserving five centuries of Assamese spiritual traditions.
heritage.description: Shaped by the shifting channels of the Brahmaputra and Subansiri rivers, Majuli is the heartland of Assamese neo-Vaishnavite culture established by Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th century. Home to 22 ancient Satras (including Kamalabari, Auniati, and Samaguri), mask-making artisans, and Mishing tribal villages.

cities.name: Sivasagar
cities.tagline: Royal Capital of the 600-Year Ahom Kingdom
cities.description: Historic capital of the legendary Ahom Dynasty who ruled Assam for 600 years without falling to the Mughals, home to the colossal Sivasagar Sivadol, Talatal Ghar palace, and Rang Ghar amphitheater.
cities.short_description: Historical capital of the Ahom kingdom, featuring ancient royal palaces and temples.

monuments.name: Rang Ghar
monuments.summary: Two-storey royal pavilion built in 1746, recognized as one of the oldest surviving royal sports amphitheaters in Asia.
monuments.description: Built by Ahom King Swargadeo Pramatta Singha in 1744–1751, Rang Ghar was the royal sporting amphitheater from where Ahom kings and nobles watched indigenous games, buffalo fights, and wrestling matches. Its unique roof is crafted like an inverted Ahom boat.

monuments.entry_fee: ₹25 (Indians), ₹300 (Foreigners)
visitor_notes: Roof shaped like an inverted Ahom royal longboat

monuments.name: Talatal Ghar
monuments.summary: Imposing 18th-century palace citadel featuring four storeys above ground and three subterranean floors with secret tunnels.
monuments.description: Constructed by King Swargadeo Rajeswar Singha in 1751–1769, Talatal Ghar served as a grand military base and palace. It was engineered with indigenous organic cements made of sticky rice and duck eggs, and featured secret subterranean escape tunnels leading to the Dikhow River.

religious_cultural.name: Sivasagar Sivadol
religious_cultural.summary: Ancient 18th-century Shiva temple whose 104-foot spire makes it one of the tallest Shiva temples in India.
religious_cultural.description: Constructed in 1734 by Queen Ambika, wife of Ahom King Swargadeo Siba Singha, Sivasagar Sivadol rises 32 meters high on the bank of the vast Borpukhuri tank. Its shikhara is crowned by a 7-foot tall pure gold dome (Kalasha).

cities.description: Historic center of Charaideo district, home to the sacred royal burial mounds (Maidams) of Ahom royalty and kings, recently inscribed as India's landmark UNESCO World Heritage site.

monuments.name: Charaideo Maidams
monuments.summary: UNESCO World Heritage Site: the monumental earthen tumuli and royal burial mounds of the Ahom dynasty.
monuments.description: Established in 1253 AD by first Ahom King Chaolung Sukaphaa as the dynasty's first capital, Charaideo was the ancestral necropolis where Ahom kings and queens were buried. The over 90 vaulted earthen mounds (Maidams) resemble Egyptian pyramids and showcase extraordinary medieval funerary engineering.

cities.name: Ranchi
cities.tagline: City of Waterfalls & Tribal Heritage Capital
cities.description: Capital of Jharkhand renowned as the City of Waterfalls, home to Dassam, Hundru, and Jonha Falls, historic Jagannath Temple, Pahari Mandir, and premier tribal museums.
cities.source_provenance: Jharkhand Tourism Development Corporation (JTDC) & Ministry of Tourism
cities.short_description: Capital of Jharkhand, famed for cascading waterfalls and rich tribal institutions.

museums.name: Birsa Munda Tribal University and Museum Area
museums.canonical_name: Birsa Munda Tribal University and Museum Area
museums.summary: Grand memorial museum and cultural complex dedicated to Bhagwan Birsa Munda and tribal freedom fighters of Jharkhand.
museums.description: Located at the historic Old Birsa Munda Central Jail in Ranchi where Bhagwan Birsa Munda breathed his last in 1900, this national memorial complex houses life-size bronze statues, interactive digital galleries, laser light and sound shows, and rich documentation of the Ulgulan freedom rebellion.
museums.short_description: National memorial museum complex commemorating Bhagwan Birsa Munda's life and legacy.
museums.detailed_description: Located at the historic Old Birsa Munda Central Jail in Ranchi where Bhagwan Birsa Munda breathed his last in 1900, this national memorial complex houses life-size bronze statues, interactive digital galleries, laser light and sound shows, and rich documentation of the Ulgulan freedom rebellion.
museums.historical_significance: Historic jail cell site where Bhagwan Birsa Munda attained martyrdom on June 9, 1900, dedicated as a national memorial.
museums.visiting_hours: 09:30 AM - 06:00 PM (Closed Mondays)
museums.opening_hours: 09:30 AM - 06:00 PM (Closed Mondays)

museums.name: Tribal Research Institute and Museum
museums.summary: Pioneering tribal ethnographic museum in Morabadi displaying lifestyle artefacts, weapons, and musical instruments of 32 tribes.
museums.description: Founded in 1953 at Morabadi, Ranchi, the Tribal Research Institute and Museum preserves and displays the rich cultural tapestry of Jharkhand's 32 tribal communities (including Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Ho, and Birhor), with life-sized dioramas, hunting gear, ornaments, musical instruments, and sacred art.
museums.short_description: Pioneering ethnographic museum chronicling the customs and arts of Jharkhand's 32 tribes.
museums.detailed_description: Founded in 1953 at Morabadi, Ranchi, the Tribal Research Institute and Museum preserves and displays the rich cultural tapestry of Jharkhand's 32 tribal communities (including Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Ho, and Birhor), with life-sized dioramas, hunting gear, ornaments, musical instruments, and sacred art.
museums.historical_significance: Established in 1953 as one of eastern India's premier anthropological and tribal research institutes.
museums.visiting_hours: 10:30 AM - 05:00 PM (Closed Sundays & Govt Holidays)
museums.opening_hours: 10:30 AM - 05:00 PM (Closed Sundays & Govt Holidays)

religious_cultural.name: Jagannath Temple Ranchi
religious_cultural.summary: Historic 17th-century hill temple built in 1691 by Thakur Ani Nath Shahdeo, mirroring Puri Jagannath architecture.
religious_cultural.description: Jagannath Temple Ranchi is a magnificent 17th-century shrine situated atop a hillock in Jagannathpur. Built in 1691 by Barkagarh king Thakur Ani Nath Shahdeo, the temple echoes the classical Kalinga architectural style of Puri and hosts an epic annual Rath Yatra fair.
religious_cultural.short_description: 17th-century hilltop Jagannath shrine mirroring Puri style, built by Barkagarh kings in 1691.
religious_cultural.detailed_description: Jagannath Temple Ranchi is a magnificent 17th-century shrine situated atop a hillock in Jagannathpur. Built in 1691 by Barkagarh king Thakur Ani Nath Shahdeo, the temple echoes the classical Kalinga architectural style of Puri and hosts an epic annual Rath Yatra fair.
religious_cultural.historical_significance: Constructed in 1691 AD by Thakur Ani Nath Shahdeo; celebrated center of Chota Nagpur devotion and annual Rath Yatra.

religious_cultural.name: Pahari Mandir
religious_cultural.summary: Sacred Shiva temple atop the 2,140-foot Ranchi Hill, famed for sweeping city vistas and Tricolour hoisting traditions.
religious_cultural.description: Pahari Mandir is a revered Shiva temple perched atop Ranchi Hill (2,140 ft above sea level), reached via 468 stone steps. It offers unmatched 360-degree views over Ranchi city and Ranchi Lake, and uniquely hoists the Indian National Flag on Independence Day and Republic Day.
religious_cultural.short_description: Revered hilltop Shiva temple reached via 468 steps with panoramic views of Ranchi.
religious_cultural.detailed_description: Pahari Mandir is a revered Shiva temple perched atop Ranchi Hill (2,140 ft above sea level), reached via 468 stone steps. It offers unmatched 360-degree views over Ranchi city and Ranchi Lake, and uniquely hoists the Indian National Flag on Independence Day and Republic Day.
religious_cultural.historical_significance: Formerly known as Phansi Tongri during colonial rule where freedom fighters were hanged; sanctified after Independence with national patriotic honors.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Dassam Falls
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Spectacular natural waterfall on the Kanchi river cascading from a height of 44 meters (144 ft) through rocky woodland.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Dassam Falls (also known as Da-song) is a picturesque waterfall located near Taimara village where the Kanchi River, a tributary of the Subarnarekha, cascades down 44 meters into a deep natural pool amidst dense forested hills of the Chota Nagpur plateau.
nature_parks_zoo.short_description: Spectacular 44-meter natural waterfall on the Kanchi river near Ranchi.
nature_parks_zoo.detailed_description: Dassam Falls (also known as Da-song) is a picturesque waterfall located near Taimara village where the Kanchi River, a tributary of the Subarnarekha, cascades down 44 meters into a deep natural pool amidst dense forested hills of the Chota Nagpur plateau.
nature_parks_zoo.historical_significance: The name Dassam is derived from Da-song in local Mundari dialect, signifying the pouring of water like ten streams falling together.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Hundru Falls
nature_parks_zoo.summary: One of Jharkhand's highest waterfalls, where the Subarnarekha River plunges 98 meters (322 ft) over jagged rocky cliffs.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Hundru Falls is the 34th highest waterfall in India, formed as the Subarnarekha River falls through an impressive 98-meter escarpment. The falling water creates a wide foaming pool surrounded by striking rock formations, making it a prime excursion hub.
nature_parks_zoo.short_description: Majestic 98-meter waterfall on the Subarnarekha River with dramatic rocky cliffs.
nature_parks_zoo.detailed_description: Hundru Falls is the 34th highest waterfall in India, formed as the Subarnarekha River falls through an impressive 98-meter escarpment. The falling water creates a wide foaming pool surrounded by striking rock formations, making it a prime excursion hub.
nature_parks_zoo.historical_significance: A quintessential geographical marvel of the Ranchi plateau, exemplifying knick-point rejuvenation in Chota Nagpur geology.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Jonha Falls
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Enchanting hanging valley waterfall descending 43 meters, famed as Gautamdhara with an adjacent Buddhist temple.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Jonha Falls, also revered as Gautamdhara, is situated where the Raru River plunges 43 meters down a hanging valley into lush ravine forests. Visitors descend about 700 steps to the base where an ancient ashram and Buddhist shrine honor Lord Buddha.
nature_parks_zoo.short_description: Scenic 43-meter hanging valley waterfall and Buddhist pilgrim center on the Raru River.
nature_parks_zoo.detailed_description: Jonha Falls, also revered as Gautamdhara, is situated where the Raru River plunges 43 meters down a hanging valley into lush ravine forests. Visitors descend about 700 steps to the base where an ancient ashram and Buddhist shrine honor Lord Buddha.
nature_parks_zoo.historical_significance: Tradition holds that Gautama Buddha bathed here; an ashram with a statue of Lord Buddha was established atop the hill overlooking the falls.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Hirni Falls
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Tranquil forest waterfall on the Ramgarha River plunging 37 meters amidst dense Sal jungles of West Singhbhum.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Hirni Falls is a tranquil natural cascade tucked deep inside the pristine Sal forests of West Singhbhum near Chaibasa. Falling from a height of 37 meters (121 ft), the Ramgarha River forms a misty natural spray against steep verdant cliffs.
nature_parks_zoo.short_description: Serene 37-meter waterfall ensconced in the dense Sal forests of West Singhbhum.
nature_parks_zoo.detailed_description: Hirni Falls is a tranquil natural cascade tucked deep inside the pristine Sal forests of West Singhbhum near Chaibasa. Falling from a height of 37 meters (121 ft), the Ramgarha River forms a misty natural spray against steep verdant cliffs.
nature_parks_zoo.historical_significance: Celebrated in local folklore for its untamed natural beauty and peaceful jungle ambiance near Chaibasa.

cities.name: Latehar
cities.tagline: Land of Pristine Wilderness & Towering Cascades
cities.description: Ecological treasure of the Chota Nagpur Plateau, encompassing Betla National Park, Palamau Tiger Reserve, the monumental Lodh Falls, and historic Chero dynasty forts.
cities.source_provenance: Jharkhand Forest, Environment & Climate Change Department & JTDC
cities.short_description: Ecological haven featuring Betla National Park, Palamau Tiger Reserve, and Lodh Falls.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Lodh Falls
nature_parks_zoo.summary: The highest waterfall in Jharkhand and 21st highest in India, dropping 143 meters (469 ft) on the Burha River.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Lodh Falls (also termed Burha Gagh) is the crown jewel of Jharkhand's waterfalls, plunging 143 meters in several majestic tiers through dense tropical moist deciduous forests of Latehar district. The roar of the cascade can be heard over 10 kilometers away.
nature_parks_zoo.short_description: Highest waterfall in Jharkhand (143 m) on the Burha River in Latehar district.
nature_parks_zoo.detailed_description: Lodh Falls (also termed Burha Gagh) is the crown jewel of Jharkhand's waterfalls, plunging 143 meters in several majestic tiers through dense tropical moist deciduous forests of Latehar district. The roar of the cascade can be heard over 10 kilometers away.
nature_parks_zoo.historical_significance: Ancient natural landmark deep within the Chota Nagpur forested plateau, revered by local indigenous communities.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Betla National Park
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Pioneering national park with dense sal forests, wild elephant herds, gaurs, and 16th-century Chero dynasty forts.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Betla National Park is one of the oldest sanctuaries in eastern India, spanning sal and bamboo forests on the Chota Nagpur Plateau. It hosts rich wildlife including Asian elephants, gaurs, sloth bears, sambars, and leopards, alongside the historical twin forts of the Chero rulers.
nature_parks_zoo.short_description: Premier national park in Latehar featuring diverse wildlife and 16th-century twin Chero forts.
nature_parks_zoo.detailed_description: Betla National Park is one of the oldest sanctuaries in eastern India, spanning sal and bamboo forests on the Chota Nagpur Plateau. It hosts rich wildlife including Asian elephants, gaurs, sloth bears, sambars, and leopards, alongside the historical twin forts of the Chero rulers.
nature_parks_zoo.historical_significance: Established in 1986; home to the twin Purana and Naya Qila forts built by Chero King Medini Ray during the 16th century.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Palamau Tiger Reserve
nature_parks_zoo.summary: One of India's original nine Project Tiger reserves, spanning 1,129 sq km of rugged hills and river valleys.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Palamau Tiger Reserve was constituted under Project Tiger in 1973 as one of India's earliest tiger conservation reserves. Spread over 1,129 sq km of valleys, plateaus, and forests drained by the North Koel and Auranga rivers, it protects leopards, elephants, and rich flora.
nature_parks_zoo.short_description: Historic Project Tiger reserve spanning 1,129 sq km of rugged Chota Nagpur wilderness.
nature_parks_zoo.detailed_description: Palamau Tiger Reserve was constituted under Project Tiger in 1973 as one of India's earliest tiger conservation reserves. Spread over 1,129 sq km of valleys, plateaus, and forests drained by the North Koel and Auranga rivers, it protects leopards, elephants, and rich flora.
nature_parks_zoo.historical_significance: Pioneering sanctuary where India's first formal tiger census via pugmark enumeration was conducted in 1932.

tourist_places.summary: The "Queen of Chotanagpur", a cool hill resort at 3,622 feet altitude famed for Magnolia Point sunset and sunrise.

tourist_places.name: Patratu Valley
tourist_places.summary: Picturesque valley renowned for dramatic winding serpentine hairpin loop roads and lush green forested hills.
tourist_places.description: Patratu Valley is famous throughout eastern India for its winding multi-tiered serpentine ghat road with hairpin loops carved into lush green hills. Viewpoints along the curves offer stunning panoramic vistas across the forested valley floor and towards Patratu Dam.
tourist_places.short_description: Spectacular serpentine ghat road and panoramic mountain valley viewpoints.
tourist_places.detailed_description: Patratu Valley is famous throughout eastern India for its winding multi-tiered serpentine ghat road with hairpin loops carved into lush green hills. Viewpoints along the curves offer stunning panoramic vistas across the forested valley floor and towards Patratu Dam.
tourist_places.historical_significance: Modern engineering marvel developed through Ramgarh district hills that has become one of Jharkhand's most photographed scenic corridors.

tourist_places.opening_hours: Open 24 Hours (Best: 06:00 AM - 06:30 PM)

tourist_places.summary: Expansive reservoir on the Nalkari River featuring the Patratu Lake Resort, speed boating, and scenic island hills.
tourist_places.description: Patratu Dam is a sprawling artificial reservoir constructed across the Nalkari and other streams, holding over 81 square kilometers of storage. Equipped with Patratu Lake Resort, jet skiing, motor boating, and sunset promenades, it is a premier family leisure destination.
tourist_places.short_description: Vast scenic reservoir and water sports resort encircled by forested hills.
tourist_places.detailed_description: Patratu Dam is a sprawling artificial reservoir constructed across the Nalkari and other streams, holding over 81 square kilometers of storage. Equipped with Patratu Lake Resort, jet skiing, motor boating, and sunset promenades, it is a premier family leisure destination.
tourist_places.historical_significance: Built in the 1960s to supply cooling water for the Patratu Thermal Power Station, subsequently developed into a premier eco-tourism hub.

cities.name: Deoghar

cities.description: Spiritual sanctuary of eastern India, revered for the Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga temple complex, sacred Shravani Mela pilgrimage, Trikut Pahar, and Tapovan caves.
cities.short_description: Revered holy destination home to the Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga and Trikut Pahar.

heritage.name: Deoghar
heritage.summary: Ancient holy destination meaning "Abode of the Gods", central to Santhal Pargana heritage, Naulakha Temple, and Tapovan.
heritage.description: Deoghar is one of eastern India's most revered cultural and spiritual hubs. Known as Baidyanath Dham, it encompasses a wealth of historic destinations including Naulakha Temple, Tapovan caves, Nandan Pahar, and Kundeshwari Temple alongside vibrant craft traditions of peda confectionary.
heritage.short_description: Historic spiritual center of Santhal Pargana, celebrated as the "Abode of the Gods".
heritage.detailed_description: Deoghar is one of eastern India's most revered cultural and spiritual hubs. Known as Baidyanath Dham, it encompasses a wealth of historic destinations including Naulakha Temple, Tapovan caves, Nandan Pahar, and Kundeshwari Temple alongside vibrant craft traditions of peda confectionary.
heritage.historical_significance: Ancient religious center documented in Puranic texts as the seat of divine physician Vaidyanatha.
heritage.visiting_hours: Open 24 Hours
heritage.opening_hours: Open 24 Hours

heritage.name: Baba Baidyanath Temple
heritage.summary: One of the revered twelve Shiva Jyotirlingas, center of the epic annual Shravani Mela Kanwariya pilgrimage.
heritage.description: Baba Baidyanath Temple complex features 22 shrines clustered around the main 72-foot stone temple housing the revered Kamana Lingam. Millions of saffron-clad Kanwariya pilgrims undertake a barefoot journey of over 100 kilometers from Sultanganj carrying holy Ganga water during the sacred month of Shravan.
heritage.short_description: Revered 12-Jyotirlinga shrine and Shakti Peetha, venue of the world-famous Shravani Mela.
heritage.detailed_description: Baba Baidyanath Temple complex features 22 shrines clustered around the main 72-foot stone temple housing the revered Kamana Lingam. Millions of saffron-clad Kanwariya pilgrims undertake a barefoot journey of over 100 kilometers from Sultanganj carrying holy Ganga water during the sacred month of Shravan.
heritage.historical_significance: According to Hindu lore, Ravana worshipped Lord Shiva here; Shiva cured his severed heads acting as divine Vaidya.

tourist_places.name: Trikut Pahar
tourist_places.summary: Trio of prominent hill peaks rising to 2,470 feet with Mayurakshi River source caves and panoramic valley views.
tourist_places.description: Trikut Pahar consists of three dramatic granite peaks named after Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh, rising 2,470 feet above sea level. Featuring historical caves where Sage Bamdev meditated, the hill is famous for panoramic views of Santhal Pargana forests and ropeway rides.
tourist_places.short_description: Three sacred peaks rising to 2,470 ft with meditation caves and sweeping valley views.
tourist_places.detailed_description: Trikut Pahar consists of three dramatic granite peaks named after Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh, rising 2,470 feet above sea level. Featuring historical caves where Sage Bamdev meditated, the hill is famous for panoramic views of Santhal Pargana forests and ropeway rides.

cities.name: Puri

cities.description: Spiritual jewel of the Char Dham pilgrimage, home to the sacred 12th-century Jagannath Temple, vibrant Golden Beach, and world-renowned Pattachitra arts.

heritage.name: Raghurajpur Heritage Crafts Village
heritage.summary: World-renowned artisan village where every household preserves the age-old master craft of Pattachitra cloth paintings.
heritage.description: Nestled amidst coconut and palm groves 14 km from Puri, Raghurajpur is India's premier heritage crafts village. Every villager is an artisan specializing in Pattachitra (cloth-based scroll painting with mineral pigments), palm leaf carvings (Talapatra Chitra), cow dung toys, and wood sculptures. It is also the birthplace of legendary Odissi maestro Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and the traditional Gotipua dance.

religious_cultural.name: Jagannath Temple
religious_cultural.summary: Sacred 12th-century temple of Lord Jagannath, one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites, celebrated for the mega Rath Yatra.
religious_cultural.description: Constructed by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva in the 12th century, this iconic temple enshrines Lord Jagannath along with brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra. The temple is famous for its towering 65-meter deula, mysterious flag fluttering opposite to wind direction, the world's largest kitchen (Ananda Bazar) preparing Mahaprasad, and the internationally celebrated annual Chariot Festival (Ratha Yatra).

monuments.name: Konark Sun Temple
monuments.summary: Monumental 13th-century UNESCO World Heritage Sun Temple sculpted as a gigantic cosmic stone chariot.
monuments.description: Built in 1250 AD by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty, Konark Sun Temple is an architectural summit of ancient Kalinga stonecraft. Designed as a mammoth chariot of the Sun God Surya, it features 24 exquisitely carved 12-spoked wheels acting as accurate astronomical sundials and seven horses galloping towards the dawn.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Chilika Lake
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Asia's largest coastal lagoon and Ramsar Wetland site, famous for playful Irrawaddy dolphins and migratory birds.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Chilika Lake covers over 1,100 square kilometers across three districts of Odisha. It supports one of the world's only two surviving populations of Irrawaddy dolphins, predominantly spotted at Satapada. During winter, Nalabana Island becomes host to over one million migratory birds arriving from Siberia, Mongolia, and Central Asia.

heritage.name: Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves
heritage.summary: Historic rock-cut cave complexes carved in the 1st-2nd century BCE under Emperor Kharavela for Jain monks.
heritage.description: The twin hills of Udayagiri (Sunrise Hill) and Khandagiri (Broken Hill) feature 33 partly artificial rock-cut caverns built during the Chedi dynasty. Udayagiri contains the famous Rani Gumpha (Queen's Cave) with two-storey reliefs, and Hathigumpha featuring the 17-line Brahmi inscription chronicling the military expeditions and civic works of King Kharavela.

monuments.name: Dhauli Shanti Stupa
monuments.summary: Striking white peace pagoda atop Dhauli Hills marking Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism and non-violence.
monuments.description: Dhauli Shanti Stupa sits beside the Daya River where the monumental Kalinga War occurred in 261 BCE. Seeing the river turn crimson with bloodshed, Emperor Ashoka renounced conquest by war (Digvijaya) in favor of conquest through dharma (Dharmavijaya). The stupa was built jointly in 1972 by the Kalinga Nippon Buddha Sangha and the Government of Odisha.

religious_cultural.name: Lingaraj Temple
religious_cultural.summary: Majestic 11th-century temple representing the pinnacle of mature Kalinga architecture, dedicated to Lord Harihara.
religious_cultural.description: The largest temple in Bhubaneswar, Lingaraj Temple stands inside a spacious compound with 108 subsidiary shrines. The central deula rises to an imposing 55 meters and is dedicated to Tribhuvaneswara (Lord of Three Worlds, Shiva combined with Vishnu as Harihara). The complex overlooks the sacred Bindusagar Lake.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Nandankanan Zoological Park
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Internationally celebrated zoological garden nestled around Kanjia Lake, famous for white tigers and lion safaris.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Nandankanan, literally meaning "Garden of Heavens", covers 437 hectares across the Chandaka forest. It was the first zoo in the world where white tigers were bred in captivity and the first to breed Indian pangolins successfully. Features open-moated enclosures, ropeway over the lake, nocturnal animal house, and boat safaris.

heritage.name: Barabati Fort
heritage.summary: 14th-century medieval citadel on the Mahanadi River, featuring an ornate stone gateway, deep moat, and earthen ramparts.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Similipal National Park
nature_parks_zoo.summary: UNESCO Biosphere Reserve boasting lush Sal forest ranges, rare pseudo-melanistic black tigers, and cascading waterfalls.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Covering 2,750 square kilometers, Similipal is the 7th largest national park in India. Named after the red silk cotton (Semul) trees that blossom here, it features dramatic escarpments, Barehipani Falls (399m) and Joranda Falls (150m), and is the only habitat on Earth hosting wild pseudo-melanistic Royal Bengal tigers.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Bhitarkanika National Park
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Vibrant mangrove estuary and Ramsar site sheltering India's largest population of giant saltwater crocodiles.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Bhitarkanika is India's second largest mangrove ecosystem after the Sundarbans, created by the rivers Brahmani, Baitarani, and Dhamra. The park is home to over 1,700 saltwater crocodiles (including record-holding specimens exceeding 20 feet), king cobras, spotted deer, wild boars, and 215 bird species.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Daringbadi
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Idyllic highland hill station named the "Kashmir of Odisha", featuring pine groves, coffee plantations, and winter frost.
nature_parks_zoo.description: Perched at an elevation of 915 meters in the Eastern Ghats of Kandhamal, Daringbadi is the only place in Odisha that occasionally experiences sub-zero temperatures and winter ground frost. Attractions include dense pine forests, lush organic coffee plantations, Hill View Point, Midubanda Waterfall, and vibrant tribal villages.

tourist_places.name: Hirakud Dam
tourist_places.summary: Engineering marvel across the Mahanadi River, the world's longest earthen dam stretching 25.8 kilometers.
tourist_places.description: Constructed between 1948 and 1957 as India's first major multipurpose river valley project after independence, Hirakud Dam forms a massive reservoir covering 743 square kilometers. Visitors can ascend Gandhi Minar and Nehru Minar watchtowers for breathtaking 360-degree views of the waters and surrounding Barapahad hills.
